newsitem.title: FRANCE: French in "record" gloom over jobs, cuts - poll.
newsitem.headline: French in "record" gloom over jobs, cuts - poll.

text.p: French people, worried about jobs and cuts, have been plunged into "record" gloom since President Jacques Chirac was elected 18 months ago, an opinion poll said on Monday.
The BVA polling institute rated morale at 37, down from 49 and the lowest mark since it started regularly probing the nation's mood 13 years ago.
The poll was the latest in a series of surveys that reported widespread disillusion with French political leaders.

Another survey last week showed that 96 percent of French voters felt "anxious or "morose" about the economic and social situation in France. Sixty-seven percent of participants said they did not believe economic recovery would come in 1997.
BVA blamed the gloom on a feeling among French people that they had done their best to help their leaders curb unemployment which has nevertheless reached record levels.
The previous low reached on the BVA scale was 39 in 1984 when the late Socialist president Francois Mitterrand launched an austerity plan in a political turnabout.
The high, happy points on the BVA scale were when Mitterrand was re-elected in 1988, at the end of the 1991 Gulf War, and when Chirac was elected.

The BVA findings coincided with a call from one of France's main trade unions for week-long protests against the centre-right government over job losses in defence, the state electricity company, banks and social welfare services.
